verification: Source text and saved evidence checked; no new simulation or optimization
interpretation: The reduced Deng-derived translated circuit is coupled to a suspended model. Stimuli lasting two baseline periods suppress two expected flexor motor bursts at each tested layer. Read left RG traces and right MN activation together. Stronger-current controls matter: a one-second PF pulse shifts motor timing by 0.208 cycle while RG timing stays unchanged. A motor shift alone therefore does not prove RG resetting. This is a translated reduced-circuit test, not original-rat locomotion replication.
